description: Explains Niño-region indices, the 2026 RONI change, Tahiti-Darwin pressure, moorings and satellites, data assimilation, multi-model ensembles, spring predictability limits, and calibrated seasonal probabilities.

related_resources.reason: Region-specific indices: Niño 3.4, Southern Oscillation, ocean-atmosphere multivariate approaches.
Standardized Tahiti-Darwin sea-level-pressure differences; negative SOI generally with El Niño, positive with La Niña.
Date and rationale of CPC shift from traditional ONI to RONI.
RONI calculation: subtract global tropical SST anomaly and normalize variance; same + or - 0.5C thresholds and historical duration criterion.
Current RONI data set, 5 overlapping-season historic criterion and cautions about provisional recent values.
Historical background and moored subsurface ocean observing systems, including TAO.
TAO started 1984, completed 1994, became TAO/TRITON in 2000, ocean sensor data in ENSO observations.
Value of subsurface observation and assimilation for tropical Pacific climate analyses.
Comparison of real-time dynamical and statistical seasonal forecasts from 2002 to 2023, spring predictability barrier and evaluation methodology.
Dated example of ensemble probabilistic seasonal outlook; does not provide timeless specific phase forecasts.
